This is a ten-minute laptop walk-through. We compare ordinary least
squares against the lasso for estimating sparse regression
coefficients, varying the sample size. **No HPC access required** —
everything runs in-process via `simulatr_check()`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(simulatr)
```

# 1. Build the parameter grid

Each row of `parameter_grid` is one problem setting. Attach the ground
truth (the true coefficient vector) to the grid via `add_ground_truth()`.

```{r}
parameter_grid <- data.frame(
  n        = c(25, 50, 75, 100),
  p        = 15,
  s        = 5,
  beta_val = 3
)

get_ground_truth <- function(p, s, beta_val) {
  beta <- numeric(p)
  beta[seq_len(s)] <- beta_val
  list(beta = beta)
}

parameter_grid <- add_ground_truth(parameter_grid, get_ground_truth)
```

# 2. Define the components

Three constructors produce typed S4 objects whose argument names are
validated against the grid at study-build time.

```{r}
lm_model <- simulatr_model(
  name = "lm_model",
  generate = function(n, p, ground_truth) {
    X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
    y <- as.numeric(X %*% ground_truth$beta + rnorm(n))
    list(X = X, y = y)
  }
)

ols <- simulatr_method(
  name = "ols",
  run = function(data) {
    fit <- lm.fit(data$X, data$y)
    list(beta = unname(fit$coefficients))
  }
)

lasso <- simulatr_method(
  name = "lasso",
  run = function(data) {
    fit <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(data$X, data$y, nfolds = 5, intercept = FALSE)
    beta_hat <- as.numeric(glmnet::coef.glmnet(fit, s = "lambda.1se"))
    list(beta = beta_hat[-1L])
  }
)

rmse <- simulatr_metric(
  name = "rmse",
  score = function(output, ground_truth) {
    sqrt(mean((output$beta - ground_truth$beta) ^ 2))
  }
)
```

# 3. Build the study

```{r}
study <- simulatr_study(
  parameter_grid   = parameter_grid,
  fixed_parameters = list(B = 20, seed = 4),
  models  = list(lm_model = lm_model),
  methods = list(ols = ols, lasso = lasso),
  metrics = list(rmse = rmse)
)
```

If a method or model named an unresolvable formal, the construction
above would have raised a precise error pointing at the offending
component.

# 4. Run, evaluate, summarise

`simulatr_check()` is the laptop one-liner: it runs the full
generate→run→evaluate pipeline at small `B` and returns a list of three
tibbles.

```{r}
out <- simulatr_check(study, B = 2)
out$summary
```

For the full simulation on a single laptop:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
results <- simulatr_run(study)
evals   <- simulatr_evaluate(study, results)
summary <- simulatr_evals_summarise(evals)
```

For a cluster, save the study with `saveRDS()` and hand it to the
[Nextflow pipeline](https://github.com/Katsevich-Lab/simulatr-pipeline).
See `vignette("running-on-a-cluster")`.

# 5. Capture session info for reproducibility

Embed `simulatr_session_info()` into any artifact you save, so a future
reviewer can verify the package and pipeline contract version that
produced it.

```{r}
info <- simulatr_session_info()
info$contract_version
info$contract_hash
```
